findings.title: Team permission check requires both admin AND owner
findings.body: In addGuests.handler.ts isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as `await isTeamAdmin(...) && await isTeamOwner(...)`. The name and intent is admin OR owner, but && requires the caller to be both at once. If roles are mutually exclusive no team member ever passes, and otherwise pure admins or pure owners are incorrectly denied with FORBIDDEN. The feature then only works for the organizer/attendee, breaking team delegation. Change && to ||.

findings.title: Duplicate and blacklist checks are case-sensitive, blacklist bypassable
findings.body: In addGuests.handler.ts the blacklist is lowercased on load but guest emails are compared verbatim: `guest === attendee.email` for duplicates and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` for blocks. Emails are case-insensitive, so Blocked@spam.com bypasses blacklist entry blocked@spam.com, and User@x.com creates a second Attendee row alongside user@x.com. Intra-request duplicates like ["a@x.com","a@x.com"] are also not deduped server-side, creating duplicate rows. Normalize with trim().toLowerCase() on both sides and dedupe the request.

findings.title: Guests array unbounded with no dedup allows email bombing
findings.body: In addGuests.schema.ts guests is defined as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no min, max, or uniqueness. Any authenticated caller allowed by the handler, including any existing attendee, can submit hundreds or thousands of addresses in one call. The handler then creates that many Attendee rows, patches calendars, and fans out that many emails. This enables DB bloat, spam/email bombing, and DoS of calendar integrations. Add min/max limits and uniqueness.

findings.title: Email helper called with unfiltered guests list
findings.body: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler filters input into uniqueGuests for the database insert but then calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the original unfiltered array. The email helper decides new vs existing via newGuests.includes(attendee.email). A re-submitted existing address is therefore misclassified as new and gets a full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, inconsistent with what was stored. Pass uniqueGuests instead of guests.

findings.title: Calendar update uses caller's credentials instead of organizer's
findings.body: In addGuests.handler.ts credentials are loaded as getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) where ctx.user is whoever called the endpoint, which can be a team admin or attendee, and used to build EventManager for updateCalendarAttendees. The calendar event belongs to the booking owner, not the caller. When a non-organizer adds guests the patch runs with the wrong OAuth tokens, fails or touches the wrong calendar, while the DB already has new attendees. This leaves database and Google/Outlook calendars diverged. Load the organizer's credentials via booking.userId.

findings.title: No guard against adding guests to cancelled or past bookings
findings.body: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler only checks that the booking exists, then inserts attendees for any bookingId. There is no check for status CANCELLED/REJECTED or endTime in the past. Adding guests to a cancelled or finished meeting still creates Attendee rows, attempts calendar patches on dead events, and sends new_guests_added emails for meetings that will never happen. Reject unless booking is active/upcoming.

findings.title: Add-guests emails ignore standard-email disable settings
findings.body: In email-manager.ts sendAddGuestsEmails takes only (calEvent, newGuests) and unconditionally emails organizer, team members, and all attendees. Unlike sendScheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails and others, it never checks disableStandardEmails metadata or host/attendee disabled flags. Workspaces that disabled standard emails for privacy or noise control will still get spammed via this path. Thread eventTypeMetadata and disabled flags through like other send functions.

findings.title: Empty-state Add button missing type button submits parent forms
findings.body: In MultiEmail.tsx the empty-state Add Emails Button has no type attribute while the other add button correctly uses type button. Inside any HTML form a button defaults to submit, so clicking to add an email row in a form using this reusable component submits the whole form instead, triggering validation or navigation. Add type="button" to that Button.

findings.title: Validation error flag never cleared on success
findings.body: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx isInvalidEmail is set true on failed validation, but the onSuccess handler only closes the dialog and clears emails without clearing the flag, and overlay/X close also leaves it set. The next time the dialog is opened the red emails_must_be_unique_valid banner is still visible despite fresh input, confusing users. Reset isInvalidEmail on success, on close, and when input changes.
